metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code with a deployable entry point (server.js with Express listener), Dockerfile, and Kubernetes deployment manifests present for a single service.
metadata.archetype_justification: GET /rates endpoint queries MongoDB with filtering parameters (read-heavy data access). POST /quote performs stateless calculation with no database writes. No CUD operations, no entity lifecycle management. Read-heavy traffic with minimal business logic.

top_gaps.gap: API key hardcoded in source code; MongoDB connection string in plaintext ConfigMap
top_gaps.impact: Critical security vulnerability — credentials exposed in version control

top_gaps.title: Managed Databases

findings.title: Managed Compute
findings.description: The application is fully containerized with a multi-stage Dockerfile (node:18-alpine) and deployed via Kubernetes manifests (Deployment with 2 replicas, resource limits, security context hardening). No IaC confirms the cluster is managed (EKS).
findings.gap: No IaC confirms the cluster is managed (EKS). K8s cluster provisioning is not visible in this repository.
findings.recommendation: Define EKS cluster provisioning in IaC (Terraform or CDK). Consider Fargate profiles for serverless container execution.

findings.title: Managed Databases
findings.description: MongoDB is referenced via a connection URL (MONGO_URL in k8s/configmap.yaml). No IaC provisions or manages the database. The mongodb driver version (1.4.7) targets MongoDB 2.4 era. No managed database service is configured.
findings.gap: Database is entirely self-managed with no automated failover, backups, or patching. No IaC defines the database infrastructure.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon DocumentDB (MongoDB-compatible) or MongoDB Atlas on AWS. Provision via IaC with Multi-AZ, automated backups, encryption at rest.

findings.title: Network Security
findings.description: K8s service uses ClusterIP (internal-only). Deployment has hardened securityContext. No NetworkPolicy restricts pod-to-pod traffic. No Ingress with TLS configured.
findings.gap: No Kubernetes NetworkPolicy limits ingress/egress traffic. No TLS termination configured.
findings.recommendation: Add a Kubernetes NetworkPolicy to restrict ingress to authorized sources and egress to MongoDB only. Configure Ingress with TLS.

findings.title: API Entry Point
findings.description: No API Gateway, ALB, or CloudFront configured. K8s service is ClusterIP with no Ingress resource. No throttling, gateway-level auth, or request validation.
findings.gap: Service exposed directly with no managed gateway or load balancer providing throttling, auth, or request validation.
findings.recommendation: Deploy an Ingress controller with API Gateway for throttling, authentication, and request validation.

findings.title: Auto-Scaling
findings.description: K8s Deployment specifies static replica count of 2. No HorizontalPodAutoscaler configured.
findings.gap: All capacity is statically provisioned — cannot respond to traffic spikes or scale down.
findings.recommendation: Add HorizontalPodAutoscaler targeting CPU utilization or request rate.

findings.title: Backup and Recovery
findings.description: No backup configuration for MongoDB. No aws_backup_plan, no backup_retention_period, no PITR. Database infrastructure not defined in IaC.
findings.gap: No automated backup or recovery mechanism. Data loss event would be unrecoverable.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to managed database with automated backups and PITR. If self-managed, implement automated backup scripts with S3 storage.

findings.title: High Availability and Fault Isolation
findings.description: K8s Deployment has 2 replicas but no topology spread constraints, pod anti-affinity, or explicit multi-AZ config. Both replicas could schedule in same AZ.
findings.gap: No AZ distribution enforced. Database HA unknown/unconfigured.
findings.recommendation: Add topologySpreadConstraints to distribute replicas across AZs. Migrate to managed database with Multi-AZ.

findings.title: Infrastructure as Code Coverage
findings.description: K8s manifests define application deployment (Deployment, Service, ConfigMap, Namespace). No IaC for database, networking, cluster, monitoring, or DNS. Coverage ~30-40%.
findings.gap: No IaC for database provisioning, cluster management, networking, monitoring, or backup.
findings.recommendation: Define IaC (Terraform or CDK) for all infrastructure dependencies: database, networking, monitoring, backup.

findings.title: CI/CD Automation
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline configuration exists. No GitHub Actions, Jenkinsfile, buildspec.yml, or .gitlab-ci.yml. All builds and deployments are manual.
findings.gap: No automated build, test, or deploy pipeline.
findings.recommendation: Implement CI/CD pipeline with stages for lint, test, build Docker image, push to ECR, deploy to K8s.

findings.title: Programming Languages
findings.description: Node.js with engines declared as 0.10.x (EOL). Dependencies: express@3.4.8 (unmaintained), mongodb@1.4.7 (EOL). Container runs Node 18 but code uses 0.10 patterns (callbacks, no async/await). No AWS SDK.
findings.gap: Compound legacy: EOL engine declaration, unmaintained Express 3.x, EOL MongoDB driver 1.x, no cloud-native SDK.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade to Node.js 20 LTS with Express 4.x, mongodb 6.x with async/await, and AWS SDK v3.

findings.title: Monolith vs Microservices
findings.description: Single 45-line server.js file contains all logic: Express app, middleware, routes, DB access, and business logic. No module boundaries or separation of concerns.
findings.gap: Tightly-coupled single-file application with all concerns interleaved. Cannot independently test, scale, or modify individual concerns.
findings.recommendation: Refactor into modular structure: separate routes, services, repositories, and middleware. This is structural refactoring, not microservices decomposition.

findings.title: API Versioning Strategy
findings.description: No API versioning. Endpoints are /rates and /quote with no version prefix, no Accept-Version headers.
findings.gap: No versioning — breaking changes affect all consumers simultaneously.
findings.recommendation: Implement URL-path versioning (e.g., /v1/rates, /v1/quote). Document API contracts in OpenAPI specification.

findings.title: Service Discovery
findings.description: MongoDB endpoint externalized via MONGO_URL env var (K8s ConfigMap). Service discoverable within cluster via K8s DNS. No formal service registry or API catalog.
findings.gap: Environment variables for endpoints but no dynamic discovery beyond K8s DNS. No API catalog.
findings.recommendation: K8s DNS provides adequate discovery for current scale. Publish OpenAPI spec to an API catalog for consumer discoverability.

findings.title: Unstructured Data Storage
findings.description: No S3 or managed object storage configured. Rate data stored in MongoDB. Service does not currently handle unstructured documents but has no infrastructure to support it if needed.
findings.gap: No managed object storage infrastructure.
findings.recommendation: If unstructured document handling is needed (shipping labels, customs documents), provision S3 with lifecycle policies. Primary gap is addressed by DocumentDB migration.

findings.title: Unified Data Access Layer
findings.description: Database access is inline within the route handler. MongoClient.connect called inside GET /rates handler — new connection per request, no pooling, no repository pattern.
findings.gap: No data access layer — connections opened per-request inside route handlers. Connection exhaustion risk, untestable without live database.
findings.recommendation: Implement repository pattern with a dedicated data access module managing a connection pool.

findings.title: Database Engine Version and EOL
findings.description: No database engine version pinned in any configuration. The mongodb driver 1.4.7 targets MongoDB 2.4/2.6, both long past EOL (2016). No version-update procedure exists.
findings.gap: Database engine version unknown/unpinned and implied to be severely EOL. No lifecycle management.
findings.recommendation: Pin database engine version in IaC when migrating to DocumentDB. Upgrade mongodb driver to version 6.x.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest
findings.description: No encryption at rest configured for MongoDB. No KMS keys, no encryption parameters. Database referenced only by connection URL with no security parameters.
findings.gap: No encryption at rest for the persistent data store.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon DocumentDB which provides encryption at rest by default using AWS KMS.

findings.title: API Authentication
findings.description: Static shared API key checked via x-api-key header middleware. Basic API key auth — not token-based (OAuth2/JWT). No identity attribution, expiration, or scope-based authorization.
findings.gap: Static API key authentication with no rotation, no per-consumer identity, no expiration.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to token-based auth (JWT/OAuth2) via Amazon Cognito or API Gateway authorizer.

findings.title: Centralized Identity Integration
findings.description: Application manages its own authentication via hardcoded API key. No external IdP (Cognito, Okta, OIDC, SAML). No SSO or federated authentication.
findings.gap: No centralized IdP integration — authentication island with static credential scheme.
findings.recommendation: Integrate with Amazon Cognito or organizational IdP for centralized authentication.

findings.title: Secrets Management
findings.description: API key is HARDCODED in source code (server.js). MongoDB connection string stored in K8s ConfigMap (not Secret) as plaintext. Credentials in version control history.
findings.gap: Plaintext credentials in source code. API key visible to anyone with repo access.
findings.recommendation: Remove hardcoded credentials. Store in AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation. Use K8s External Secrets Operator.

findings.title: Compute Hardening and Patching
findings.description: No patching automation or vulnerability scanning. Dockerfile uses node:18-alpine (major version only). No Dependabot, no Renovate, no container scanning. Known-vulnerable dependencies in use.
findings.gap: No automated patching. No vulnerability scanning. Dependencies have known vulnerabilities.
findings.recommendation: Add Dependabot or Renovate. Enable ECR image scanning. Pin base image to digest. Upgrade dependencies.

findings.title: Application Security Pipeline
findings.description: No security scanning tools configured. No CI/CD pipeline exists. No SAST, DAST, dependency scanning, or container scanning.
findings.gap: Zero security scanning — vulnerabilities in outdated dependencies go undetected.
findings.recommendation: Include npm audit, SAST (Semgrep), and ECR scanning in CI/CD. Add Dependabot for automated updates.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing
findings.description: No distributed tracing instrumentation. No OpenTelemetry, no X-Ray, no trace ID propagation.
findings.gap: No tracing — cannot diagnose latency or trace requests to MongoDB.
findings.recommendation: Add OpenTelemetry SDK with automatic Express and MongoDB instrumentation.

findings.title: SLO Definitions
findings.description: No SLO definitions, no CloudWatch alarms, no monitoring configuration. No defined acceptable service levels.
findings.gap: No SLOs — cannot measure whether service meets user expectations.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs for p99 latency, availability, and error rate. Implement monitoring to track compliance.

findings.title: Business Metrics
findings.description: No custom metrics published. No CloudWatch, StatsD, or Prometheus metrics. Only default container-level metrics from K8s platform.
findings.gap: No business metrics — cannot track quote volume, rate lookups, or error rates by endpoint.
findings.recommendation: Publish custom metrics: quotes/min, rate lookups/min, error rates, response time percentiles.

findings.title: Anomaly Detection and Alerting
findings.description: No alerting configured. No CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection, no PagerDuty/OpsGenie integration.
findings.gap: No alerting — degradation or outage has no automated detection or notification.
findings.recommendation: Configure CloudWatch alarms on error rate and p99 latency with anomaly detection. Set up alerting integration.

findings.title: Deployment Strategy
findings.description: K8s Deployment uses default RollingUpdate with readiness/liveness probes on TCP port 8080. Rolling deploys with health checks but no traffic shifting.
findings.gap: No canary or blue/green. Cannot validate new versions with subset of traffic.
findings.recommendation: Implement canary deployments using Argo Rollouts or Flagger with progressive traffic shifting.

findings.title: Integration Testing
findings.description: No tests of any kind. No unit tests, integration tests, or e2e tests. No test script in package.json, no test framework dependency.
findings.gap: Zero automated test coverage. Regression risk is maximum.
findings.recommendation: Add integration tests with Jest/Supertest for /rates and /quote endpoints. Run in CI pipeline.

findings.title: Incident Response Automation
findings.description: No runbooks, no incident response automation, no self-healing patterns beyond K8s liveness probe restarts.
findings.gap: Incident response entirely ad hoc — no documented procedures for common failure modes.
findings.recommendation: Create runbooks for common incidents: DB connectivity loss, pod OOM, high latency.

findings.title: Observability Ownership
findings.description: No observability ownership. No CODEOWNERS, no per-service dashboards, no alarms with owners, no SLO definitions with team attribution.
findings.gap: No one explicitly responsible for monitoring service health.
findings.recommendation: Define CODEOWNERS. Create service-level dashboard. Assign alarm ownership.

evaluations.title: Workflow Orchestration
evaluations.reason: Score 4 — data-gateway archetype. No multi-step workflows exist in the read path. Workflow orchestration is not applicable by design.

evaluations.title: Async Messaging and Streaming
evaluations.reason: Score 4 — data-gateway archetype. Synchronous reads dominate and are the correct design. No write-back or indexing flows exist.

evaluations.title: Async vs Sync Communication
evaluations.reason: Score 4 — data-gateway archetype. Sync reads are correct; no write-back or cache invalidation flows exist.

evaluations.title: Long-Running Process Handling
evaluations.reason: Score 4 — data-gateway archetype. No user-facing operations exceed 30 seconds. Simple query and calculation only.

evaluations.title: Stored Procedures and Schema Complexity
evaluations.reason: Score 4 — No stored procedures or proprietary SQL. All business logic in application layer.

evaluations.title: Audit Logging
evaluations.reason: has_iac_provisioning_aws_resources=false. This repo contains application-level K8s manifests only. CloudTrail evaluation belongs in foundation infrastructure repo.

evaluations.title: Resource Tagging Governance
evaluations.reason: has_iac_provisioning_aws_resources=false. This repo provisions no AWS resources — nothing to tag.

decomposition_strategy.rationale: The application is a 45-line single-file micro-service with 2 endpoints. Microservices decomposition would be over-engineering. Refactoring into separated concerns (routes, services, repositories) is the appropriate level of modularization.
